schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PAYROLL (SSNO INT, DEPTNO INT);
CREATE TABLE APPLICANT (SSNO INT, JOBTITILE INT, OFFICENO INT);
q1: SELECT Y.* FROM PAYROLL AS X, APPLICANT AS Y WHERE X.SSNO = Y.SSNO AND X.DEPTNO = 29
q2: SELECT C.* FROM PAYROLL AS A, (SELECT Y.SSNO, Y.DEPTNO FROM PAYROLL AS Y) AS B, APPLICANT AS C WHERE A.SSNO = B.SSNO AND C.SSNO = A.SSNO AND B.DEPTNO = 29

explanation: Q1 filters PAYROLL records with DEPTNO=29 and joins with APPLICANT. Q2 joins PAYROLL with a subquery (B) from PAYROLL, requiring B.DEPTNO=29. This allows Q2 to include APPLICANT records even if PAYROLL has multiple entries for the same SSNO with DEPTNO=29, leading to duplicate rows in Q2 when multiple PAYROLL rows match, unlike Q1 which returns one row per APPLICANT.
